title: Diagonal orbital-count/heat-kernel asymptotic for Kleinian groups from a one-pair polynomial heat lower bound
difficulty_reason: Allow the named heat-kernel existence, Dirichlet spectral theorem, Dodziuk exhaustion convergence, explicit H3 heat kernel, classical Delsarte formula and Eskin-McMullen averaging input. Substantive uniform estimates remain: the Selberg ball-integral representation is used to control both spectral regimes, with domain-independent transform coefficients, a relative low-frequency error uniform below beta log(rho)/rho and polynomial decay above that threshold. The resulting split is implemented on all sufficiently large bounded domains and passed through the noncompact exhaustion; the application also constructs uniform image-sum tail and near-point heat ratios, then propagates a single-pair lower bound to compact sets. These actual analytic estimates support one H2 core. The spectral theorem, epsilon bookkeeping, classical appendix and direct terminal corollary are supporting inputs/closure, not separate advanced units or a reason for H3.
